## Lab digital twin skill

### Package root

This skill ships **inside** the relocatable twin package (`.agents/skills/lab-digital-twin/`).  
When the package sits in a monorepo, a copy may also live at monorepo `.agents/skills/`.

Standards of truth (paths relative to package root):

- `docs/STANDARD.md` — how to build **any** lab machine twin
- `AGENTS.md` — agent rules
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — runtime layout
- `standards/machine_template.md` — checklist for machine #2+

## What is in scope

| Path                               | Role                         |
| ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `software/viewer/`                 | Live Three.js student app    |
| `software/controller/`             | Python state machine + tests |
| `cad/cq/`                          | Optional CadQuery            |
| `docs/` + `standards/`             | Specs and process            |
| `.agents/skills/lab-digital-twin/` | This skill                   |

## Out of scope

Parent monorepo experiments (`impressive_demo.py`, root `build_*_centrifuge.py`, etc.) unless the user explicitly asks.

## Daily commands

```bash
# from package root
./scripts/serve.sh          # http://127.0.0.1:8765/viewer/
./scripts/test.sh
```

After viewer edits: bump `?v=` cache busters; hard-refresh the browser.

## Conventions (do not break)

1. Package stays **self-contained** — no required imports from monorepo parent.
2. Live 3D is **procedural** `centrifuge3d.js`, not GLB-only.
3. Nameplate letters are **S R E** (not SSS).
4. Lid hinge rear (+Z); front of machine −Z; Y-up.
5. Tube access only when lid open and rotor stopped.
6. Match Python controller semantics when changing JS run logic.
7. New machines: follow `docs/STANDARD.md` + `standards/machine_template.md`.

## Adding a new instrument

1. Create `<name>_twin/` using STANDARD §2 layout.
2. Fill product brief from `standards/machine_template.md`.
3. Spec controls → Python tests → viewer.
4. Lab environment in-scene.
5. Optional CAD library.
6. Pass STANDARD §7 quality bar.
7. Ensure `./scripts/serve.sh` works after moving the folder.

## Cleanup policy

Do not commit: `__pycache__`, `.venv`, `.venv-cq`, screenshot spam, experimental badge crops under `export/renders/`.
Prefer documented exports only (`product_preview.png`, `lcd_sample.png`). _(digital, skill, package)_

  machine. _(student, softwareviewer, threejs)_

- If not provided or if target language definition is ambiguous, ask for examples of valid strings to be parsed
  _(provided, target, language)_
- Before developing the pyparsing expressions, define a Backus-Naur Form definition and save this in docs/grammar.md.
  Update this document as changes are made in the parser. _(developing, pyparsing, expressions)_
- Import pyparsing using `import pyparsing as pp`, and use that for all pyparsing references. _(import, pyparsing,
  import)_
- If referencing names from `pyparsing.common`, follow the pyparsing import with "ppc = pp.common" and use `ppc` as the
  namespace to access `pyparsing.common`. _(referencing, names, pyparsingcommon)_
- If referencing names from `pyparsing.unicode`, follow the pyparsing import with "ppu = pp.unicode" and use `ppu` as
  the namespace to access `pyparsing.unicode`. _(referencing, names, pyparsingunicode)_
- When writing parsers that contain recursive elements (using `Forward()` or `infix_notation()`), immediately enable
  packrat parsing for performance: `pp.ParserElement.enable_packrat()` (call this right after importing pyparsing). See
  <https://pyparsing-docs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/HowToUsePyparsing.html>. _(writing, parsers, contain)_
- For recursive grammars, define placeholders with `pp.Forward()` and assign later using the `<<=` operator; give
  Forwards meaningful names with `set_name()` to improve errors. _(recursive, grammars, define)_
- Use PEP8 method and argument names in the pyparsing API (`parse_string`, not `parseString`). _(method, argument,
  names)_
- Do not include expressions for matching whitespace in the grammar. Pyparsing skips whitespace by default. _(include,
  expressions, matching)_
- For line-oriented grammars where newlines are significant, set skippable whitespace to just spaces/tabs early:
  `pp.ParserElement.set_default_whitespace_chars(" \t")`, and define `NL = pp.LineEnd().suppress()` to handle line ends
  explicitly. _(lineoriented, grammars, newlines)_
- Use `set_name()` on all major grammar elements to support railroad diagramming and better error/debug output.
  _(setname, major, grammar)_
- The grammar should be independently testable, without pulling in separate modules for data structures, evaluation, or
  command execution. _(grammar, independently, testable)_
- Results names should take the place of numeric indexing into parsed results in most places. _(results, names,
  numeric)_
- Define results names using call format not `set_results_name()`, example:
  `full_name = Word(alphas)("first_name") + Word(alphas)("last_name")` _(define, results, names)_
- If adding results name to an expression that is contains one more sub-expressions with results names, the expression
  must be inclused in a Group. _(adding, results, expression)_
- Use `pp.CaselessKeyword`/`pp.CaselessLiteral` when keywords should match regardless of case.
  _(ppcaselesskeywordppcaselessliteral, keywords, match)_
- When the full input must be consumed, call `parse_string` with `parse_all=True`. _(input, consumed, parsestring)_
- If the grammar must handle comments, define an expression for them and use the `ignore()` method to skip them.
  _(grammar, handle, comments)_
- Use pyparsing `Group` to organize sub-expressions. Groups are also important for preserving results names when a
  sub-expression is used in a `OneOrMore` or `ZeroOrMore` expression. _(pyparsing, group, organize)_
- Suppress punctuation tokens to keep results clean; a convenient pattern is
  `LBRACK, RBRACK, LBRACE, RBRACE, COLON = pp.Suppress.using_each("[]{}:")`. _(suppress, punctuation, tokens)_
- Use pyparsing `Each()` to define a list of elements that may occur in any order. _(pyparsing, define, elements)_
- The '&' operator is the operator form of Each and is often more readable when combining order-independent parts.
  _(operator, operator, readable)_
- Use parse actions to do parse-time conversion of data from strings to useful data types. _(parse, actions, parsetime)_
- For quoted strings, use `pp.dbl_quoted_string().set_parse_action(pp.remove_quotes)` to unquote automatically.
  _(quoted, strings, ppdblquotedstringsetparseactionppremovequotes)_
- Map reserved words to Python constants per this example for parsing "true" to auto-convert to a Python True:
  `pp.Keyword("true").set_parse_action(pp.replace_with(True))` (and similarly for false/null/etc.). _(reserved, words,
  python)_
- Use "using*each" with a list of keywords to define keyword constants, instead of separate assignments.*(usingeach,
  keywords, define)\_
- Choose the appropriate matching method: _(choose, appropriate, matching)_
- `parse_string()` parses from the start _(parsestring, parses, start)_
- `search_string()` searches anywhere in the text _(searchstring, searches, anywhere)_
- `scan_string()` yields all matches with positions _(scanstring, yields, matches)_
- `transform_string()` is a convenience wrapper around `scan_string` to apply filters or transforms defined in parse
  actions, to perform batch transforms or conversions of expressions within a larger body of text _(transformstring,
  convenience, wrapper)_
- For line suffixes or directives, combine lookahead and slicing helpers: `pp.FollowedBy(...)` with `pp.rest_of_line`;
  when reusing a base expression with a different parse action, call `.copy()` before applying the new action to avoid
  side effects. _(suffixes, directives, combine)_
- When defining a parser to be used in a REPL: _(defining, parser)_
- add pyparsing `Tag()` elements of the form `Tag("command", <command-name>)` to each command definition to support
  model construction from parsed commands. _(pyparsing, elements, tagcommand)_
- define model classes using dataclasses, and use the "command" attribute in the parsed results to identify which model
  class to create. The model classes can then be used to construct the model from the ParseResults returned by
  parse*string(). Define the models in a separate parser_models.py file.*(define, model, classes)\_
- If defining the grammar as part of a Parser class, only the finished grammar needs to be implemented as an instance
  variable. _(defining, grammar, parser)_
- `ParseResults` support "in" testing for results names. Use "in" tests for the existence of results names, not
  `hasattr()`. _(parseresults, support, testing)_
- Avoid left recursion where possible. If you must support left-recursive grammars, enable it with
  `pp.ParserElement.enable_left_recursion()` and do not enable packrat at the same time (these modes are incompatible).
  _(avoid, recursion, possible)_
- Use `pp.SkipTo` as a skipping expression to skip over arbitrary content. _(ppskipto, skipping, expression)_
- For example, `pp.SkipTo(pp.LineEnd())` will skip over all content until the end of the line; add a stop*on argument to
  SkipTo to stop skipping when a particular string is matched.*(example, ppskiptopplineend, content)\_
- Use `...` in place of simple SkipTo(expression) _(simple, skiptoexpression)_
- Use the pyparsing `ParserElement.run_tests` method to run mini validation tests. _(pyparsing, parserelementruntests,
  method)_
- Pass a single multiline string to `run_tests` to test the parser on multiple test input strings, each line is a
  separate test. _(single, multiline, string)_
- You can add comments starting with "#" within the string passed to `run_tests` to document the individual test cases.
  _(comments, starting, within)_
- To pass test input strings that span multiple lines, pass the test input strings as a list of strings. _(input,
  strings, multiple)_
- Pass `parse_all=True` to `run_tests` to test that the entire input is consumed. _(parsealltrue, runtests, entire)_
- When generating unit tests for the parser: _(generating, tests, parser)_
- generate tests that include presence and absence of optional elements _(generate, tests, include)_
- use the methods in the mixin class pyparsing.testing.TestParseResultsAsserts to easily define expression, test input
  string, and expected results _(methods, mixin, class)_
- do not generate tests for invalid data _(generate, tests, invalid)_
- If troubleshooting parse actions, use pyparsing's `trace_parse_action` decorator to echo arguments and return value
  _(troubleshooting, parse, actions)_
- During development, call `pp.autoname_elements()` to auto-assign names to unnamed expressions to improve `dump()` and
  error messages. _(during, development, ppautonameelements)_
- Sub-expressions can be tested in isolation using `ParserElement.matches()` _(subexpressions, tested, isolation)_
- When defined out of order, Literals can mistakenly match fragments: `Literal("for")` will match the leading "for" in
  "format". Can be corrected by using `Keyword` instead of `Literal`. _(defined, order, literals)_
- Dump the parsed results using `ParseResults.dump()`, `ParseResults.pprint()`, or `repr(ParseResults)`. _(parsed,
  results, parseresultsdump)_

---

- Never Object.assign(mesh.position, …) — use position.set. Extrude hole winding must be opposite the outer path or the
  deck hole fails. Full solid body box blocks the chamber; use hollow walls + deck hole. Camera on +Z shows the back of
  a front=−Z machine. Panel tilt around center sinks the panel into the body; pivot at top, geometry outside. Fill
  upper-front corner gaps with bulkhead + pillars after cutting lower front only. Multi-material LCD: keep texture on
  lcdMat, not mesh.material array. Shared materials on keys mean one glow lights all keys — clone per key. Cache-bust
  module imports while developing. CadQuery on bleeding-edge Python often fails; pin 3.12 for CQ.
  _(objectassignmeshposition, positionset, extrude)_

- text OPEN key ┌──────────► LIDOPEN ◄──────────┐ │ │ close lid │ │ ▼ │ │ READY │ │ START/SHORT │ │ ▼ │ │ ACCEL
  ──────────────┤ fault │ ▼ │ │ RUN │ │ time end / STOP │ │ ▼ │ │ DECEL │ │ ▼ │ │ END ──auto open──► LIDOPEN │ │ │ └──►
  READY (if auto-open disabled) │ └── faults: ERR (from any spinning state → DECEL then fault hold) _(lidopen, close,
  ready)_
- | State | Rotor | Lid | Display status | | ------------ | ----------- | --------------- | -------------- |
  ------------------------- | | LIDOPEN | 0 | unlocked/open | OPEN | | READY | 0 | closed locked | READY | | ACCEL |
  increasing | locked | ACCEL | | RUN | at setpoint | locked | RUN | | DECEL | decreasing | locked | BRAKE | | END | 0 |
  may auto-unlock | END | | ERRLID | 0 | — | E-01 | | ERRIMBALANCE | braking | locked | E-02 | | ERRTACHO | braking |
  locked | E-03 | | ERROVERSPEED | braking | locked | E-04 | | ERRMOTOR | braking | locked | E-05 | _(state, rotor,
  display)_ |
- START only from READY (lid closed, no fault). OPEN only when rpmactual == 0 and not in ACCEL/RUN/DECEL. Closing lid
  (sensor) moves LIDOPEN → READY. STOP from ACCEL/RUN → DECEL. SHORT: while held, behave as RUN at setpoint; release →
  DECEL. Imbalance inject: from ACCEL/RUN → DECEL then ERRIMBALANCE. Run complete (timer): DECEL → END → optional auto
  lid open → LIDOPEN. Clear error: STOP long-press or OPEN when stopped → READY/LIDOPEN. _(start, ready, closed)_

- When writing parsers that contain recursive elements (using Forward() or infixnotation()), immediately enable packrat
  parsing for performance: pp.ParserElement.enablepackrat() (call this right after importing pyparsing). See
  <https://pyparsing-docs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/HowToUsePyparsing.html>. (writing, parsers, contain) _(writing,
  parsers, contain)_
- For recursive grammars, define placeholders with pp.Forward() and assign later using the <<= operator; give Forwards
  meaningful names with setname() to improve errors. (recursive, grammars, define) _(recursive, grammars, define)_
- Use PEP8 method and argument names in the pyparsing API (parsestring, not parseString). (method, argument, names)
  _(method, argument, names)_
- Do not include expressions for matching whitespace in the grammar. Pyparsing skips whitespace by default. (include,
  expressions, matching) _(include, expressions, matching)_
- For line-oriented grammars where newlines are significant, set skippable whitespace to just spaces/tabs early:
  pp.ParserElement.setdefaultwhitespacechars(" \t"), and define NL = pp.LineEnd().suppress() to handle line ends
  explicitly. (lineoriented, grammars, newlines) _(lineoriented, grammars, newlines)_

  organize)_

- Generated with pypdf (+ cryptography for encrypted PDFs) from files in ../manuals/. _(generated, pypdf, cryptography)_
- Regenerate: _(regenerate)_
- bash cd centrifugetwin source .venv/bin/activate or: .venv/bin/python python - <<'PY' from pathlib import Path from
  pypdf import PdfReader _(centrifugetwin, source, venvbinactivate)_
- manuals = Path("research/manuals") out = Path("research/manualsextracted") out.mkdir(existok=True) for p in
  manuals.glob(".pdf"): r = PdfReader(str(p)) if r.isencrypted: r.decrypt("") text = "\n".join( f"\n===== PAGE {i+1}
  =====\n{(page.extracttext() or '')}" for i, page in enumerate(r.pages) ) (out / f"{p.stem}.txt").writetext(text,
  encoding="utf-8") print(p.name, len(r.pages), "pages") PY _(manuals, pathresearchmanuals,
  pathresearchmanualsextracted)_
- If not provided or if target language definition is ambiguous, ask for examples of valid strings to be parsed
  _(provided, target, language)_
- Before developing the pyparsing expressions, define a Backus-Naur Form definition and save this in docs/grammar.md.
  Update this document as changes are made in the parser. _(developing, pyparsing, expressions)_
- Import pyparsing using `import pyparsing as pp`, and use that for all pyparsing references. _(import, pyparsing,
  import)_
- If referencing names from `pyparsing.common`, follow the pyparsing import with "ppc = pp.common" and use `ppc` as the
  namespace to access `pyparsing.common`. _(referencing, names, pyparsingcommon)_
- If referencing names from `pyparsing.unicode`, follow the pyparsing import with "ppu = pp.unicode" and use `ppu` as
  the namespace to access `pyparsing.unicode`. _(referencing, names, pyparsingunicode)_
- When writing parsers that contain recursive elements (using `Forward()` or `infix_notation()`), immediately enable
  packrat parsing for performance: `pp.ParserElement.enable_packrat()` (call this right after importing pyparsing). See
  <https://pyparsing-docs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/HowToUsePyparsing.html>. _(writing, parsers, contain)_
- For recursive grammars, define placeholders with `pp.Forward()` and assign later using the `<<=` operator; give
  Forwards meaningful names with `set_name()` to improve errors. _(recursive, grammars, define)_
- Use PEP8 method and argument names in the pyparsing API (`parse_string`, not `parseString`). _(method, argument,
  names)_
- Do not include expressions for matching whitespace in the grammar. Pyparsing skips whitespace by default. _(include,
  expressions, matching)_
- For line-oriented grammars where newlines are significant, set skippable whitespace to just spaces/tabs early:
  `pp.ParserElement.set_default_whitespace_chars(" \t")`, and define `NL = pp.LineEnd().suppress()` to handle line ends
  explicitly. _(lineoriented, grammars, newlines)_
- Use `set_name()` on all major grammar elements to support railroad diagramming and better error/debug output.
  _(setname, major, grammar)_
- The grammar should be independently testable, without pulling in separate modules for data structures, evaluation, or
  command execution. _(grammar, independently, testable)_
- Results names should take the place of numeric indexing into parsed results in most places. _(results, names,
  numeric)_
- Define results names using call format not `set_results_name()`, example:
  `full_name = Word(alphas)("first_name") + Word(alphas)("last_name")` _(define, results, names)_
- If adding results name to an expression that is contains one more sub-expressions with results names, the expression
  must be inclused in a Group. _(adding, results, expression)_
- Use `pp.CaselessKeyword`/`pp.CaselessLiteral` when keywords should match regardless of case.
  _(ppcaselesskeywordppcaselessliteral, keywords, match)_
- When the full input must be consumed, call `parse_string` with `parse_all=True`. _(input, consumed, parsestring)_
- If the grammar must handle comments, define an expression for them and use the `ignore()` method to skip them.
  _(grammar, handle, comments)_
- Use pyparsing `Group` to organize sub-expressions. Groups are also important for preserving results names when a
  sub-expression is used in a `OneOrMore` or `ZeroOrMore` expression. _(pyparsing, group, organize)_
- Suppress punctuation tokens to keep results clean; a convenient pattern is
  `LBRACK, RBRACK, LBRACE, RBRACE, COLON = pp.Suppress.using_each("[]{}:")`. _(suppress, punctuation, tokens)_
- Use pyparsing `Each()` to define a list of elements that may occur in any order. _(pyparsing, define, elements)_
- The '&' operator is the operator form of Each and is often more readable when combining order-independent parts.
  _(operator, operator, readable)_
- Use parse actions to do parse-time conversion of data from strings to useful data types. _(parse, actions, parsetime)_
- For quoted strings, use `pp.dbl_quoted_string().set_parse_action(pp.remove_quotes)` to unquote automatically.
  _(quoted, strings, ppdblquotedstringsetparseactionppremovequotes)_
- Map reserved words to Python constants per this example for parsing "true" to auto-convert to a Python True:
  `pp.Keyword("true").set_parse_action(pp.replace_with(True))` (and similarly for false/null/etc.). _(reserved, words,
  python)_
- Use "using*each" with a list of keywords to define keyword constants, instead of separate assignments.*(usingeach,
  keywords, define)\_
- Choose the appropriate matching method: _(choose, appropriate, matching)_
- `parse_string()` parses from the start _(parsestring, parses, start)_
- `search_string()` searches anywhere in the text _(searchstring, searches, anywhere)_
- `scan_string()` yields all matches with positions _(scanstring, yields, matches)_
- `transform_string()` is a convenience wrapper around `scan_string` to apply filters or transforms defined in parse
  actions, to perform batch transforms or conversions of expressions within a larger body of text _(transformstring,
  convenience, wrapper)_
- For line suffixes or directives, combine lookahead and slicing helpers: `pp.FollowedBy(...)` with `pp.rest_of_line`;
  when reusing a base expression with a different parse action, call `.copy()` before applying the new action to avoid
  side effects. _(suffixes, directives, combine)_
- When defining a parser to be used in a REPL: _(defining, parser)_
- add pyparsing `Tag()` elements of the form `Tag("command", <command-name>)` to each command definition to support
  model construction from parsed commands. _(pyparsing, elements, tagcommand)_
- define model classes using dataclasses, and use the "command" attribute in the parsed results to identify which model
  class to create. The model classes can then be used to construct the model from the ParseResults returned by
  parse*string(). Define the models in a separate parser_models.py file.*(define, model, classes)\_
- If defining the grammar as part of a Parser class, only the finished grammar needs to be implemented as an instance
  variable. _(defining, grammar, parser)_
- `ParseResults` support "in" testing for results names. Use "in" tests for the existence of results names, not
  `hasattr()`. _(parseresults, support, testing)_
- Avoid left recursion where possible. If you must support left-recursive grammars, enable it with
  `pp.ParserElement.enable_left_recursion()` and do not enable packrat at the same time (these modes are incompatible).
  _(avoid, recursion, possible)_
- Use `pp.SkipTo` as a skipping expression to skip over arbitrary content. _(ppskipto, skipping, expression)_
- For example, `pp.SkipTo(pp.LineEnd())` will skip over all content until the end of the line; add a stop*on argument to
  SkipTo to stop skipping when a particular string is matched.*(example, ppskiptopplineend, content)\_
- Use `...` in place of simple SkipTo(expression) _(simple, skiptoexpression)_
- Use the pyparsing `ParserElement.run_tests` method to run mini validation tests. _(pyparsing, parserelementruntests,
  method)_
- Pass a single multiline string to `run_tests` to test the parser on multiple test input strings, each line is a
  separate test. _(single, multiline, string)_
- You can add comments starting with "#" within the string passed to `run_tests` to document the individual test cases.
  _(comments, starting, within)_
- To pass test input strings that span multiple lines, pass the test input strings as a list of strings. _(input,
  strings, multiple)_
- Pass `parse_all=True` to `run_tests` to test that the entire input is consumed. _(parsealltrue, runtests, entire)_
- When generating unit tests for the parser: _(generating, tests, parser)_
- generate tests that include presence and absence of optional elements _(generate, tests, include)_
- use the methods in the mixin class pyparsing.testing.TestParseResultsAsserts to easily define expression, test input
  string, and expected results _(methods, mixin, class)_
- do not generate tests for invalid data _(generate, tests, invalid)_
- If troubleshooting parse actions, use pyparsing's `trace_parse_action` decorator to echo arguments and return value
  _(troubleshooting, parse, actions)_
- During development, call `pp.autoname_elements()` to auto-assign names to unnamed expressions to improve `dump()` and
  error messages. _(during, development, ppautonameelements)_
- Sub-expressions can be tested in isolation using `ParserElement.matches()` _(subexpressions, tested, isolation)_
- When defined out of order, Literals can mistakenly match fragments: `Literal("for")` will match the leading "for" in
  "format". Can be corrected by using `Keyword` instead of `Literal`. _(defined, order, literals)_
- Dump the parsed results using `ParseResults.dump()`, `ParseResults.pprint()`, or `repr(ParseResults)`. _(parsed,
  results, parseresultsdump)_

## Preferences & Style

> Personal tastes, language preferences, opinions, and personality

- Prefer operator forms for readability: use +, |, ^, ~, etc., instead of explicit And/MatchFirst/Or/Not classes (see
  Usage notes in <https://pyparsing-docs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/HowToUsePyparsing.html>). _(prefer, operator, forms)_
- Prefer `Keyword` over `Literal` for reserved words to avoid partial matches (e.g., `Keyword("for")` will not match the
  leading "for" in "format"). _(prefer, keyword, literal)_
- For comma-separated sequences, prefer `pp.DelimitedList(...)`; wrap with `pp.Optional(...)` to allow empty lists or
  objects where appropriate. _(commaseparated, sequences, prefer)_
- Use objects defined in pyparsing.common for common types like integer, real — these already have their conversion
  parse actions defined. _(objects, defined, pyparsingcommon)_
- When you want native Python containers from the parse, use `pp.Group(..., aslist=True)` for lists and
  `pp.Dict(..., asdict=True)` for dict-like data. _(native, python, containers)_
- When extending, prefer small deterministic geometry helpers (box, cyl, makeCable, deckWithHole) over opaque imported
  black-box models until the interaction model is stable. _(extending, prefer, deterministic)_
- Prefer operator forms for readability: use +, |, ^, ~, etc., instead of explicit And/MatchFirst/Or/Not classes (see
  Usage notes in <https://pyparsing-docs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/HowToUsePyparsing.html>). _(prefer, operator, forms)_
- Prefer `Keyword` over `Literal` for reserved words to avoid partial matches (e.g., `Keyword("for")` will not match the
  leading "for" in "format"). _(prefer, keyword, literal)_
- For comma-separated sequences, prefer `pp.DelimitedList(...)`; wrap with `pp.Optional(...)` to allow empty lists or
  objects where appropriate. _(commaseparated, sequences, prefer)_
- Use objects defined in pyparsing.common for common types like integer, real — these already have their conversion
  parse actions defined. _(objects, defined, pyparsingcommon)_
- When you want native Python containers from the parse, use `pp.Group(..., aslist=True)` for lists and
  `pp.Dict(..., asdict=True)` for dict-like data. _(native, python, containers)_

- Interactive fidelity beats CAD purity. Prefer a procedural Three.js product model that wires cleanly to controls over
  a heavy GLB that is hard to animate. One behavioral truth. Document states in controlspec.md. Python tests lock safety
  interlocks; JS implements the same transitions for the app. CAD is a library, not the runtime. STEP/BOM for
  documentation and future manufacturing; GLB optional for marketing stills. Lab context in-scene. Floor, walls,
  lighting, benches — never a pure black void for student builds. Samples when relevant. Tubes/fluids with before/after
  separation layers teach procedure, not just buttons. _(interactive, fidelity, beats)_
- Auto-open lid on successful end is optional but good for training UX. _(autoopen, successful, optional)_
- | Concern | Convention | | ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
  ------------------------------ | | Units | ≈ 100 mm per scene unit; Y-up; front of instrument = −Z | | Modules |
  app.js logic + UI; 3d.js geometry; sfx.js audio | | Keys | Textured keycaps with labels; userData.keyId for picking |
  | LCD | Canvas texture, updated each frame from snap() | | Lab | buildLabRoom() or equivalent environment group | |
  Demo | Continuous loop: load → close → run → show → next material | | Cache | ?v=YYYYMMDD-note on module imports when
  shipping changes | | Dependencies | CDN Three.js via import map — no bundler required | _(concern, convention, units)_
  |
- | Concern | Convention | | --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
  ------------------------------- | | Kernel | CadQuery + OCP on Python 3.12 | | Origin | Documented once in
  dimensions.md (chamber axis, floor Z=0, mm) | | Part IDs | Stable A01…, E03… style names in STEP + PARTSMAP | |
  Fasteners | Shared library under cad/cq/lib/ or cad/library/ | | Export | STEP assembly + per-part STEP; STL mesh
  groups; optional GLB | _(concern, convention, kernel)_ |
